column1: # Ledger edits that are carried but not yet landed.
# The ledger is one shared file under one lease, so an agent that has carried a
# row but cannot take the lease stages it here instead of holding the file open
# between batches. Apply the whole queue with
#     python3 conformance/flip-row.py --from-queue conformance/queued-ledger-edits.tsv
# and verify it without writing the ledger with the same command plus --check,
# which reports how many rows would change and leaves the file's sha alone.
# A row is removed once it lands: the tsv's own rust column is the record from
# then on, and a file that holds landed rows reads as pending work.
# Do not add a row here without its witness already in the tree. flip-row.py
# refuses a `ported` row with an empty rust column, so a queue entry is a claim
# that the test exists.
# Batch 1, thirty rows, landed in 8ea093f: thirteen newly carried in
# Schema.test.ts, seven carrying the allOf intersections in
# fromJsonSchemaDocument.test.ts, ten re-points of rows that were already
# `ported` while citing the wrong witness, and eight excusals of rows whose
# bodies assert nothing at runtime. `git show 8ea093f -- conformance/behavior-tests.tsv`
# is the batch.
# path
# Landed (60 rows in one call) after BoldKite released the ledger lease.
# Batch 2, seven rows from elm-effect-rs-port-managedruntime-oupl. Witnesses live in
# crates/elm-effect/tests/managed_runtime.rs (7 tests, all green). Queue staged
# because BoldKite holds the ledger lease for elm-effect-rs-sgze and did not answer
# a request-release; landed once the lease was free.
# Batch 3, twenty-one rows from elm-effect-rs-port-txpriorityqueue-69y4 (landed). Witnesses in
# crates/elm-effect/tests/tx_priority_queue.rs (21 tests, green under --features stm).
# Batch 4, five rows from elm-effect-rs-port-schema-a2c (landed): the
# resolveAnnotations / resolveAnnotationsKey getters. Witnesses in
# crates/elm-effect-schema/tests/schema_annotations.rs (8 tests, green).
# Batch 5, six rows from elm-effect-rs-port-schema-a2c (landed): the brand and
# fromBrand describes. Witnesses in
# crates/elm-effect-schema/tests/schema_transform.rs (green).
# Batch 6, twenty-one rows from elm-effect-rs-port-schema-a2c (landed): the top-level
# constructor rows at :5216-:5586. Six are carried (the four StringFrom*
# transforms, whose witnesses are in tests/schema_transform.rs and whose
# implementations are in src/transform.rs; plus the two DateTimeUtc rows whose
# wire side is a string or a number the port already has). Fifteen are
# excused because the row's wire value is a JS/Effect value type with no
# Unknown variant, each named in its own reason rather than as one block.
# Batch 7, forty rows from elm-effect-rs-port-schema-a2c (staged, awaiting the lease
# IcyCoast holds for conformance/behavior-tests.tsv): the Class / TaggedClass /
# Error / TaggedError describes at :6802-:7791 and the extend rows under them.
# Witnesses in crates/elm-effect-schema/tests/schema_class.rs, 21 tests, green
# under `cargo test -p elm-effect-schema`. Rows the port cannot witness stay
# open rather than excused: the immer and `[immerable]` describes (:6961-:7064,
# :7247), the JS object-model legs (`instanceof`, `_a` class-body fields), the
# `verifyGeneration` arbitrary leg, and `assertInclude(err.stack, ...)` (:7503,
# :7558, :7646's stack half).
# Batch 8, nine rows from elm-effect-rs-port-schema-a2c (staged, awaiting the
# lease): the TemplateLiteralParser describe at :6599-:6783, all of it. Witnesses
# in crates/elm-effect-schema/tests/schema_template.rs (37 tests, green). Four of
# the nine needed real port work: a part now captures by its own kind (a literals
# part captures the value, a nested parser its list, a nested template literal
# the text it matched), and the parser's encode runs each capture back through
# its part, so the pin's "Expected an integer at [0]" and "length of at least 1
# at [2]" refusals are ported rather than dropped.
# Batch 9, thirteen rows from elm-effect-rs-port-schema-a2c (staged, awaiting the
# lease): the Schema.makeFilter describe at :9199-:9398, all of it. Witnesses in
# crates/elm-effect-schema/tests/schema_filters.rs (14 tests, green). New surface
# in crates/elm-effect-schema/src/filters.rs: FilterOutcome (pass, bare false,
# one issue, an array), FilterIssue (a message at a relative path), FilterSpec
# (predicate, annotations, abort) and Schema::filtered, plus two SchemaError
# variants (FilterFailed, Composite) so an "all issues" decode can report a
# filter's own message at the path it pointed at.
# Batch 10, eight rows from elm-effect-rs-port-schema-a2c (staged, awaiting the
# lease): Char, Int, Natural, the four case schemas and the version-specific
# isUUID row, Schema.test.ts:10108-10361. Witnesses in
# crates/elm-effect-schema/tests/schema_refinements.rs (8 tests, green); the
# surface is crates/elm-effect-schema/src/refinements.rs. A case schema decodes
# through the transformation and encodes through the check, so decoding
# normalizes and encoding insists the value was already normalized, which is what
# all four case rows assert.
# Three rows right beside these stay open on purpose: :10319 isStringBigInt,
# :10328 isStringSymbol and :10348 isUUID assert
# `resolveAnnotations(schema)?.representation` as a structured {id, payload}
# object, and this port has no representation annotation yet. Claiming them
# would be claiming a shape that is not there.
# Batch 11, four carried rows and five excused, all from
# elm-effect-rs-port-schema-a2c (landed): the Record
# describe's key-schema rows. Witnesses in
# crates/elm-effect-schema/tests/schema_records.rs (4 tests, green). The port
# grew a per-record excess policy (`Schema::record2_excess`) and a numeric
# reading of a wire key, so `Record(Int, ...)` selects the names that spell a
# number while `"1.1"`, `"Infinity"` and `"NaN"` are unmatched keys.
# Four rows beside them stay open rather than excused, each for its own reason:
# :4159 `Record(SnakeToCamel, NumberFromString)` needs key renaming and a
# last-key-wins order that a sorted map does not preserve; :4082 puts a symbol in
# the key union; :4223 and :4231 are the `mutableKey` spelling, which has no
# analogue here though the decode they assert holds.
# Batch 12, two carried rows and four excused, from
# elm-effect-rs-port-schema-a2c (landed): the Union
# describe's dispatch rows that this port can actually witness. Witnesses in
# crates/elm-effect-schema/tests/schema_union.rs (2 tests, green, no source
# change: member order and the `oneOf` count were already the port's behaviour).
# Six rows beside them stay open, each naming what it needs:
# :4504 and :4551 are unions with a RECOVERING member (`catchDecoding` /
# `catchEncoding`), which this port does not have; :4793 and :4807 need
# sentinel-based member exclusion with the union's own message; :4821 and :4845
# need sentinel dispatch that reports the selected member's own error
# (`Missing key at ["a"]`) rather than the union-level one.
